## Auth model

There's exactly one auth mechanism: `AuthMiddleware` (`src/user/auth.middleware.ts:13`), applied **per-module via `forRoutes()`**. There are no guards, and `main.ts` registers no global guard. So the default is public — a route is protected only if it's explicitly listed in some module's `configure()`.

## Public endpoints (global prefix `/api`)

**Intentionally public — matches the RealWorld spec:**

| Endpoint | Source |
|---|---|
| `GET /api` | `src/app.controller.ts:5` |
| `POST /api/users` (register) | `src/user/user.controller.ts:32` |
| `POST /api/users/login` | `src/user/user.controller.ts:43` |
| `GET /api/tags` | `src/tag/tag.module.ts:17` — `configure()` is empty |
| `GET /api/articles` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:24` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:38` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:43` |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `src/profile/profile.controller.ts:18` |

These read an optional user via the `@User()` decorator, which falls back to decoding the JWT itself when present (`src/user/user.decorator.ts:12`) — that's deliberate optional-auth.

Also public: **`GET /docs`** (Swagger UI, `src/main.ts:18`). Note it's registered outside the `/api` prefix, so it's exposed even if you firewall `/api`.

## The one that looks unintentional

**`DELETE /api/users/:slug`** — `src/user/user.controller.ts:37`

`UserModule`'s middleware config (`src/user/user.module.ts:20`) covers only `{path: 'user', GET}` and `{path: 'user', PUT}`. The path `users/:slug` matches neither, so this route has no auth at all. It calls `userService.delete(params.slug)`, which deletes by **email** (`src/user/user.service.ts:83`) — so an unauthenticated `DELETE /api/users/victim@example.com` destroys that account. Every other mutating route in the app is listed in a `forRoutes()` block; this one is the sole omission, which is why I'd read it as an oversight rather than a design choice.

## Related, though not strictly "without logging in"

Several routes *are* behind the middleware but do no ownership check, so any logged-in user can act on anyone's data:

- `PUT /api/articles/:slug` and `DELETE /api/articles/:slug` — service takes only the slug, never compares against the author (`src/article/article.service.ts:190`, `:197`)
- `DELETE /api/articles/:slug/comments/:id` — same; the controller never passes a user id (`src/article/article.controller.ts:84`)

Worth flagging since the practical impact is similar, but the fix is different: authentication is wired up, authorization is missing.

Want me to fix the `DELETE /api/users/:slug` gap? The minimal change is adding it to `forRoutes()` in `user.module.ts`, though given the handler takes an arbitrary email, scoping it to the authenticated user instead would be the sounder fix.
